title: Machine learning screening finds unknown hepatitis C carriers in prospective deployment
summary: An XGBoost model was trained on retrospective records of 492,290 members of an Israeli health organization (0.1% active HCV carriers) and reached an AUROC of 0.95. It was then applied prospectively to over 1.5 million screening-eligible members with staged outreach, and the abstract reports a number needed to screen of 10 against 1,029 for concurrent testing of USPSTF-eligible members. The study is from a single health organization.
ai_technology: XGBoost model on electronic health record data
organization: Clalit Health Services; Ben-Gurion University; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Yield of model-guided outreach and testing compared with concurrent testing of USPSTF-eligible members after prospective deployment.
evidence.unknown: Single health organization; long-term outcomes not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost model ranking members by risk of unknown active HCV infection.
